stylised.title: Grown-up, painted
stylised.lede: A painted portrait with ink lines: a real adult woman, drawn by hand, not rendered. This is the 'grown-up face' you asked to see.
stylised.why: She is the most clearly grown-up and the warmest of the four. Even at 90 px she reads as a calm, kind teacher in her thirties, and nothing about her says cartoon. Both blind judges read her as a schoolteacher aged roughly 25 to 40. Neither found anything childish or glamorous. Her voice is a real human voice, and the most human face is the one least likely to clash with it.
stylised.risk: She is the hardest of the four to animate. Painted skin has brush texture and the light is baked in, so stretching it for a blink, an open mouth or a head turn can smear the paint. Done badly, she looks like an animated photograph, which is creepy. Today's rig fills hidden skin with smooth colour; that suits flat styles, not this one. Her skin is more orange than the Monk 6 band (see Evidence). Her first thinking frame read as a side-eye and had to be redone.

anime.title: Mature anime
anime.lede: Your suggestion: soft cel-shaded anime with adult proportions, in the manner of grown-up anime films, not school or idol anime.
anime.why: She looks confident and composed, with a defined jaw, a real nose and calm eyes. She is not a big-eyed girl. Flat cel shading is the easiest painted style to rig: colour areas cut cleanly, and hidden areas can be filled without the image model. Both judges read her as a schoolteacher aged roughly 25 to 38, never childish.
anime.risk: At rest she looks cool, even a little aloof; her warmth has to come from the smile frame and from motion. The hard shadow down one side of her nose dominates at chip size, and it has to move correctly when her head turns. Some parents may see 'anime' as a teenage hobby style; we have not tested that. Her first thinking frame read as disapproving because her brows were knitted, so it was redone with level brows.

line.title: Line of light, in lamplight
line.lede: The Instrument round's portrait, redrawn for Prakash: warm umber lines on a lamp-lit face, with a lamp-gold rim on the window side. It is the same drawing code and mouth curves, aged up and dressed in the same saree.
line.why: She is already a puppet. The six frames are settings of one vector drawing, so her identity holds exactly. She weighs a few kilobytes, stays sharp at any size and costs nothing to animate. Her skin is the closest of the four to Monk 6.
line.risk: An agent drew her in code, and agent-drawn faces have a measured quality ceiling (rejected.md: rj-agent-authored-stylised-face). Next to the painted options she looks plain, close to 'basic', the word you used. The judges read her as the oldest of the four (see the table). Her skin matches Monk 6 only because I picked the colour.

world.title: Lamplight flat (my addition)
world.lede: A fourth option I added: Asha drawn in Prakash's own light model. Flat shapes, violet shadows (never black), lamp-gold light and almost no outlines, the same way the scenes around her are built.
world.why: Every other option is a different art style from the world she lives in. This one is made the way Prakash's scenes are made, so she belongs to the window instead of looking pasted onto it. That is the audit's top complaint: the teacher is a sticker. Flat colour shapes are the easiest to rig: cuts are clean, and hidden areas fill with flat colour, as today's rig already does. She stays readable even at 38 px.
world.risk: She looks the youngest of the four (both judges: 25 to 35), so she sits closest to the age floor. Her skin is the most orange as generated, the furthest from Monk 6, and needs a colour grade. Her lips are a little dark and could read as lipstick. A flat 'vector people' style can look generic unless the rig and the light are done with care. Her first thinking frame read as a side-eye and was redone, and some edits zoomed out the framing, which the rig has to correct.
